summary: Configured daily logrotate for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 (7 compressed rotations via copytruncate so the app can keep writing), verified functionally including a full 8-day retention simulation, then restarted node1 and confirmed the config, boot identity change, and rotation behavior all survived the reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: no active process held /var/log/inventory/app.log open, confirming copytruncate (not a reload signal) is the correct continue-writing strategy
Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, copytruncate, dateext
Validated config with logrotate -d (dry run, no errors)
Forced a live rotation and confirmed app.log was truncated (copytruncate) while a new .gz rotation appeared, and that writes continued immediately after
Simulated 9 days of prior rotations and forced a 10th to confirm logrotate retains exactly 7 compressed rotations, pruning the oldest
Restored a clean baseline app.log and confirmed cron.daily/logrotate (which runs /etc/logrotate.conf, including logrotate.d/*) wires the job into daily execution

Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and rotation health, issued sudo -n shutdown -r now on node1, polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot_id, then re-verified config presence, a fresh forced rotation, and continued writability post-reboot

evidence.requirement: logrotate config created: daily, 7 compressed rotations, app.log
evidence.summary: Config written to /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate; dry run passed with no errors

evidence.requirement: exactly 7 compressed rotations retained, oldest pruned
evidence.summary: 9 synthetic prior-day rotations + 1 forced rotation resulted in exactly 7 app.log-*.gz files, with the two oldest removed

evidence.requirement: application can continue writing after rotation (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: After forced rotation, app.log was truncated to 0 bytes but remained writable; subsequent writes succeeded immediately, both pre- and post-reboot
/etc/cron.daily/logrotate (present, executable) invokes /etc/logrotate.conf, which includes /etc/logrotate.d/* where the new config lives

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594 and confirmed logrotate config/dry-run health prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: sudo -n shutdown -r now issued via backgrounded nohup; connection closed by remote host confirming the reboot took effect

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: changed boot identity proof
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 6e7da6a3-03d2-411a-85bd-c26d07cd5c9b, differing from the pre-restart 8336c3a1-... value

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of required config/service
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: logrotate config intact, dry run clean, forced rotation produced a new compressed file, and app.log accepted writes immediately after, and cron.daily/logrotate remained executable
